description: Call this right before choosing or buying an API plan: it returns, for each plan, whether it meets every condition, the monthly cost, and the official sentence behind each verdict. Use this when: the user wants to know which API plans (web scraping, SERP, web search, browser infrastructure, transactional email, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, document parsing) fit a monthly workload, budget or required conditions, or what one would cost per month at that workload. Do not use this when: the user wants to scrape, search the web, send email, generate speech, transcribe audio or parse a document itself (this tool reads no pages and calls no provider), needs proxies only, or asks about an API outside these fields. Call it right before you choose or buy a tool or plan; format "brief" returns a short answer. Find API plans (web scraping, SERP, web search, browser infrastructure, transactional email, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, document parsing) that meet required conditions: monthly pages by type (plain HTML, JavaScript rendering, blocked sites that need premium proxies), monthly searches, concurrency, requests per minute, monthly budget before tax, billing type, exit-IP countries, search engines, search-result countries and parsed result types, pages per crawl, data storage region and structured (JSON) or AI extraction. Browser infrastructure is asked in monthly browser hours, transactional email in monthly emails, text-to-speech in monthly characters, speech-to-text in monthly audio hours and document parsing in monthly document pages, each with its own conditions (for example session length, dedicated IP, voice cloning, Korean, live or recorded audio, speaker labels, pages per document, table extraction, batch discount). For search APIs it also checks the agent connection: an official or remote (hosted) MCP server and how it signs in (API key or OAuth), zero data retention on the plan, a SOC 2 report, and whether results carry the page text. Returns each plan's monthly cost, whether it meets every required condition, and for every condition met / not met / unknown with the official source sentence and check date, plus a purchase link. Plans with an unknown required condition are listed separately as partial matches. If nothing matches, returns how many plans each condition excluded and the cheapest plan that meets all the other conditions. When a plan the user has hits its limit or runs out of credits, pass alternatives_to with that plan to get other providers' plans that meet the same conditions, with how each does on the conditions the current plan misses. The optional question is the user's own words; it is read only for words that suggest a condition the request does not carry (returned as request_may_omit) and is not judged or stored. If you already have candidate plans or providers (for example from a web search), pass them as providers (search) or offer_ids (check_conditions) so that only those are judged. Hosts that support MCP Apps show the result as a comparison card. Prices are as of the as_of date of the result; call again right before buying; when you quote a result to the user, give its result_page. Example: 50,000 SERP searches a month in GB under $100; 300 hours of Korean audio a month with speaker labels.

ai_extraction_pages.description: How many of the pages need their fields extracted by an AI model (from a prompt or a schema, or automatically) without writing selectors. Each page counts in one of the two extraction fields.

alternatives_to.description: A plan the user has that hit its limit or ran out of credits, as a plan id, plan name or pricing-page URL (read as check_conditions reads plans). The search then returns the plans of other providers that meet the same conditions, ordered by cost, with how each does on the conditions this plan does not meet. Without product_types, only plans of the same field as this plan are searched. An ambiguous name returns the candidate plans in alternatives_to instead of results.

billing_types.description: Acceptable billing: monthly_subscription (A plan with a fixed fee (or minimum commitment) billed every month.) annual_subscription (A plan paid for a year at a time.) pay_as_you_go (No plan fee; a price per unit of use, billed after use or drawn from a balance topped up with any amount.) prepaid_credits (Money paid before use: a credit pack, a balance topped up first, or a plan amount charged in advance for the period.) Free plans always qualify.

browser_seconds_per_page.description: Browser time per page in seconds, for headless-browser products billed by time. Every plan must then serve pages that take this long: a hosted browser does, a request-based API only when one request may run that long.

captcha_solving.description: The plan must solve CAPTCHAs for the browser sessions (the vendor does it, not the buyer own service).

data_regions.description: Regions where data must be stored or processed, e.g. ["EU"]. Different from exit-IP countries.

detail.description: summary returns one source sentence per fact; full returns every recorded fact and sentence.

exit_ip_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of countries the page requests must exit from, e.g. ["US","DE"]. For search results of a country use search_countries.

failed_requests_not_billed.description: Requests that fail on the provider side (timeouts, blocks, 5xx) must not be billed. A flat monthly price for unlimited requests meets it, since no request is billed on its own; when only success-based billing will do, use only_successful_requests_billed.

format.description: brief returns, per plan, the plan, provider, whether it meets all, the monthly cost and the requested conditions only, each with its verdict, a one-line reason, one source sentence and its source (about a quarter of the full size); the verdicts and costs are those of full. Call it right before choosing or buying a plan.

limit.description: Maximum plans returned in each list (default and maximum 5).

max_monthly_cost_usd.description: Monthly budget in USD before tax. Compared with listed prices; annual plans use their per-month equivalent.

max_overage_usd_per_1k.description: The most the plan may charge for each 1,000 emails beyond its included volume, in USD, for transactional email. A plan whose extra price is not published as a per-1,000 figure is unknown.

mcp_auth.description: Ways to authenticate to the provider's hosted MCP endpoint, any one of which will do: api_key, oauth. Met when the endpoint accepts at least one of them; implies a hosted endpoint.

min_concurrency.description: Minimum number of concurrent requests (or browsers) the plan must allow.

min_log_retention_days.description: Days the plan must keep the logs or events of sent email where the account can read them, for transactional email. Longer retention sold as an add-on does not count.

min_pages_per_crawl.description: Pages one crawl job (from one start URL, following links) must be able to reach. A plan whose crawl has no page cap meets any number; give the size of the largest site to crawl. Different from the monthly page total.

min_pages_per_doc.description: Pages one document may have at the most the plan allows, for document parsing. Met when the stated limit is at least this many (or the pages say there is no page limit); a plan whose pages do not state a limit is unknown. The limit of the largest way of sending (batch or asynchronous) counts.

min_requests_per_minute.description: Minimum request rate the plan must allow, per minute.

min_sending_domains.description: Sending domains the plan must let one account authenticate, for transactional email. Met when the stated limit is at least this many (or the pages say it is unlimited); a plan whose pages do not state a limit is unknown.

min_session_minutes.description: Minutes one browser session must be able to run on this plan, for hosted browsers. Met when the stated longest session of the plan is at least this long; a plan whose pages do not state a session limit is unknown, and a limit the page gives only for another plan is not met.

monthly_audio_hours.description: Hours of audio transcribed per month, for speech-to-text APIs (Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Speechmatics, Amazon Transcribe, Google Cloud, OpenAI). A price given per minute is multiplied by 60. It is the whole workload: give it instead of monthly_pages, monthly_searches, monthly_browser_hours, monthly_emails and monthly_characters, not with them. Only speech-to-text products can serve it; other products are out of scope.

monthly_browser_hours.description: Browser time per month in hours, for hosted browsers (Browserbase, Browserless) billed by browser time. It is the whole workload: give it instead of monthly_pages, monthly_searches and browser_seconds_per_page, not with them. Only browser products can serve it; other products are out of scope.

monthly_characters.description: Characters of text voiced per month, for text-to-speech APIs (ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Deepgram Aura, OpenAI, Google Cloud, Amazon Polly, Azure, Gradium, Rime, Inworld, MiniMax, Murf, Hume). It is the whole workload: give it instead of monthly_pages, monthly_searches, monthly_browser_hours and monthly_emails, not with them. Only text-to-speech products can serve it; other products are out of scope.

monthly_document_pages.description: Pages of documents parsed per month, for document-parsing APIs (LlamaParse, Reducto, Unstructured, Mistral OCR, LandingAI, Amazon Textract, Google Document AI, Azure Document Intelligence, Datalab, Mathpix, Mindee, Nanonets, Upstage). A price given per credit is multiplied by the credits one page costs. It is the whole workload: give it instead of monthly_pages, monthly_searches, monthly_browser_hours, monthly_emails, monthly_characters and monthly_audio_hours, not with them. Only document-parsing products can serve it; other products are out of scope.

monthly_emails.description: Emails sent per month, for transactional email APIs (SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Resend, Amazon SES, Brevo, Mailtrap, Loops). It is the whole workload: give it instead of monthly_pages, monthly_searches and monthly_browser_hours, not with them. Only email products can serve it; other products are out of scope.

monthly_pages.description: Pages per month by type: plain_html (static pages), javascript (needs rendering), premium_proxy (blocked sites that need residential/premium proxies), javascript_premium_proxy (both).

monthly_pages_total.description: Total pages per month when the split by type is not known yet. Costs and verdicts then cover every share of JavaScript-rendered pages from 0% to 100% of the total (no premium proxies), and the result lists monthly_pages under needs_input.

monthly_searches.description: Search requests per month (one results page each).

needs_batch.description: The plan must transcribe recorded audio (a file or a stored recording), for speech-to-text. A plan priced for live audio only is not met.

needs_batch_discount.description: An official page must say a batch or asynchronous way of sending documents costs less than the list price on the plan, for document parsing. The budget and the cost are judged at the list price, not at the batch price.

needs_commercial_use.description: The plan must allow commercial use of the generated audio, for text-to-speech. A free plan limited to non-commercial use does not count; a plan whose pages do not say is unknown.

needs_dedicated_ip.description: The plan must come with a dedicated sending IP address, for transactional email. A dedicated IP sold only as an add-on on top of the plan, or only on another plan, does not count.

needs_diarization.description: The plan must label who spoke (speaker diarization), for speech-to-text. Where the vendor charges extra for it, the extra price is added to the monthly cost; where the pages state no price or no inclusion the plan is unknown.

needs_inbound.description: The service must receive email for the buyer and hand it on (inbound parsing, routes), for transactional email.

needs_korean.description: The service must voice Korean text (text-to-speech) or transcribe Korean speech (speech-to-text).

needs_no_min_billing.description: An official page must say audio is billed by the second (or an increment of seconds) with no minimum billed duration per request, for speech-to-text. A page that says nothing about rounding is unknown.

needs_no_training.description: An official page must say the vendor does not use the buyer's text, audio or documents to train its models without the buyer opting in. A use that is on by default with an opt-out to ask for does not count.

needs_official_mcp.description: The provider must publish its own MCP server (hosted by it or run by the buyer), stated in its official documentation. A server only a third party published does not count.

needs_recurring_free_tier.description: The plan must be usable every month without paying (a free plan with a monthly allowance or a monthly free credit).

needs_remote_mcp.description: The provider must host a remote MCP endpoint (a URL an MCP client connects to). An official server that can only be run on the buyer own machine does not meet it.

needs_soc2.description: The provider must hold a SOC 2 report: true for Type I or Type II, "II" for Type II.

needs_streaming.description: The service must return audio in real time as it is made (streaming or a WebSocket), for text-to-speech; for speech-to-text, it must transcribe live audio as it arrives. A speech-to-text price line is per mode, so a plan priced for recorded audio only is not met.

needs_table_extraction.description: The service must return the tables of a page as structure (rows and cells), not only the text, for document parsing.

needs_voice_cloning.description: The plan must let the account clone a voice from its own recording, for text-to-speech. Cloning limited to eligible customers, a request form or an enterprise plan does not count for a plan that is not that plan.

needs_zdr.description: Zero data retention must be usable on this plan. A provider that offers it only on a custom enterprise agreement does not meet it on its listed plans.

only_successful_requests_billed.description: Billing must count successful requests only: each successful request is charged (or draws credits) and failed ones cost nothing. A flat monthly price for unlimited requests does not meet it, since the price is the same whatever succeeds.

persistent_profiles.description: The plan must keep browser profiles (login state, cookies) between sessions.

preferred.description: Nice-to-have conditions; they do not filter, they break ties.

alternatives_to.description: Only with alternatives_to: the plan the alternatives are for and the conditions it does not meet. When the name fits several plans (status "ambiguous") or none, candidates or note say so and the lists of plans are empty.

blocked.description: The required conditions this plan does not meet or cannot confirm, with the official sentence and check date; empty when it meets them all.

quote.description: The official sentence that states the value, when the pages state it.

source.description: Official page the sentence was found on.

meets_all.description: Whether this plan meets every required condition of the call.

monthly_cost.description: status, usd, and low, high or lower_bound when they differ; for the request of this call.

answer.description: One sentence that opens the answer: the lowest-cost plan that meets every required condition with its link, or, when none does, the closest plan with what it does not meet or what is unknown, and its link. The plan is written as a markdown link, [Provider Plan](visit link), at the end of the sentence.
